resources.string: Clears com.miui.powerkeeper data without root via Shizuku. For Xiaomi / POCO / Redmi.
Connect Shizuku first — the three items below must turn green.

1. Install Shizuku (button in the connection block or Google Play).
2. Enable “Developer options” → “Wireless debugging” (Android 11+).
3. In Shizuku: “Start” → “Pair via code”, enter the code from the wireless debugging panel.
4. Come back here and tap “Grant”.
Pull down the shade → pencil (“Edit”) → in custom tiles find “Clear PowerKeeper” → drag it up. One tap on the tile clears the data; the result arrives as a notification.

• Activity-control and battery-saver profiles are reset — the system recreates the data; you do this at your own risk.\n• After a reboot Shizuku stops: turn wireless debugging back on and start it again (10 seconds).

Joyose controls Game Turbo and temperature. Removing it may cause overheating in games. You can bring it back with “Restore Joyose”. Continue?

Power and performance (PowerKeeper) stores a memory of throttling — the system past decisions about frequency. Because of it, even when you manually set 120 FPS in a game, the system may keep 60 FPS out of habit, and that is annoying. Clearing the data resets that memory: profiles are recreated from scratch and FPS limits are applied honestly.\n\nJoyose handles Game Turbo and temperature control. Removing it slightly raises the temperature threshold — the body may get warmer in games, that is expected and normal.

It does not hurt the hardware and does not break the phone: critical overheat protection is built into the kernel and works independently of Joyose.

Advice: do not play while the phone is charging and already hot. Let it cool down first and only then plug it in — the battery will live longer and throttling will not come back.

Everything is at your own risk. Restoring Joyose and recreating PowerKeeper data are one tap away — nothing here is irreversible.

LiteVer does not collect or send any data. The app has no internet access, no analytics and no ads.
